title: Simultaneous Gain-Profile Sets for Ordered Outcomes under Monotone Response and Joint-Odds Sensitivity
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR (triage, round 0) — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The analytic bounds and one-facet comparison, however, apply only to one fixed observed law, while the all-margin result is a finite LP projection and dual of the kind covered by existing discrete-causal optimization methods
The confidence region is a conservative cell-band projection with no width analysis, and the package provides no application showing that the benchmark separation changes a substantive conclusion.

Add He--Li (2026, §§2--4) to the positioning: it studies ordinal unit-level benefit under unconfoundedness with a copula association sensitivity parameter (and a distinct Rosenbaum-style analysis), so it does not subsume the typewise JSM+MTR profile, but its omission from related_work leaves the closest recent ordinal sensitivity follow-up unaddressed.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the benchmark sharp joint and marginal gain-profile polygons, their one-facet relation, causal witnesses, binary minimality, an all-finite-alphabet polytope characterization, and an all-Gamma squared-gain separation. The D0.5 math referee passed, but the general result was judged a standard finite LP projection and the explicit facets remained tied to one observed law; the field novelty floor was not met. An open-neighborhood sharp facet theorem and stronger inferential or applied payoff remain unproved.
tldr: For every feasible finite ordered outcome alphabet, the typewise joint-odds model under monotone response yields an exact simultaneous gain-profile polytope, an attained two-potential support formula, and a finite full-law vertex algorithm. Conditional profiles aggregate by a probability-weighted Minkowski sum when covariate strata have no coupling restrictions. At the specified three-level law, both the joint and full marginal-odds-plus-MTR profiles have exact all-\(g\) polygon descriptions. The joint profile is precisely the marginal profile cut by one additional compatibility halfspace; this cut excludes feasible marginal profiles for every finite \(g>1\), although the models have identical sharp ATE and individual-tail bounds.
gap: Joint-odds sensitivity results define the selection model and provide scalar or marginal-envelope results; generic discrete-causal programs can compute support values after encoding this model. An explicit linked-array dual, a single simultaneous exact-gain image with full-law attainment, and its analytic all-sensitivity benchmark phase theorem remain unstated in the audited theorem texts.
fill: Establish the exact two-potential dual and finite sharp polygon algorithm for every feasible three-level observed law, specialize it to the complete benchmark phase theorem, prove all-sensitivity scalar coincidence and the full-region separation, establish binary minimality, and give a conservative simultaneous outer confidence construction.
